item.title: Trump leaves China without meeting Kim Jong-un as trilateral summit raises concerns across Asia
item.description: The US, Chinese and Russian leaders pledged to hold talks on nuclear risk reduction, but made no mention of North Korea in their joint peace declaration.

item.title: Euronews Verify: Is Hungary turning the page on its rule of law problems?
item.description: Hungary is under new leadership, and reforms are underway. But can Péter Magyar restore the rule of law and win back the EU's trust?

item.title: US: Protesters warn of AI bubble as Anthropic makes stock market history
item.description: Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut with a record-breaking IPO valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion. Outside the exchange in New York, police detained three protesters warning of financial risks.

item.title: On board with Frontex: Euronews patrols the waters off Crete as migrant arrivals from Libya rise
item.description: Aboard the Latvian patrol vessel Valpas, Euronews follows maritime operations and visits a Frontex drone base at Tympaki airfield. A search for missing migrants near Chrissi Island highlights the dangers of the crossing, while temporary reception facilities face growing pressure.

item.title: Trump questions Europe's billions in Ukraine aid during surprise call
item.description: The US president reportedly called into a meeting of Kyiv's European allies from Air Force One, hours after talks with Putin and Xi, and said Moscow was ready to negotiate a peace deal.

item.title: Middle East conflict poses biggest threat to global energy security in history, IEA warns
item.description: Disruption to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz is driving up costs for households, while the agency says the longer the crisis continues, the harder it will be for global energy markets to recover.

item.title: Anthropic shares open 34% above IPO price in Nasdaq debut after record listing
item.description: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday, 34% above their $83 IPO price, putting the Claude maker on track for a $2 trillion valuation (€1.8tn) after it raised $81.3 billion (€74bn) in the largest initial public offering in history.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Trump, Putin and Xi hold talks as Ukraine allies meet in Berlin
item.description: Trump, Putin and Xi sign a joint declaration in China with no breakthrough on Ukraine, European leaders meet US envoys in Berlin, Spain’s election rivals debate, and COP31 talks enter their final stretch in Turkey.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 19th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 19th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Iraq orders armed factions to withdraw from strategic area amid alleged oil smuggling and US pressure
item.description: Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi has given the Iran-backed group until Friday to leave Jurf al-Nasr, as Baghdad faces growing pressure from Washington to bring powerful militias under state control.

item.title: From Carthage to Grenoble: 'Les Carthagi'Noix' opens a window on Arab culture in France
item.description: In a city renowned for its walnut trees, and at a cultural distance that surpasses geography, a group of culture and art lovers chose to begin a new story called the dialogue between the Arab world and France.

item.title: EU health chief pelted with 'ashes' by pesticide protesters
item.description: Two protesters threw what appeared to be ashes at EU Health Commissioner during a cancer summit in Brussels, prompting a strong condemnation from von der Leyen.

item.title: MWC26 Doha ushers the IQ era defined by connectivity and inclusion
item.description: FOCUS heads to GSMA’s MWC26 in Doha, where AI readiness, cloud computing and the road to 6G networks take centre stage. Running alongside the ITU’s Plenipotentiary Conference for the first time, the event brings together 194 member states to advance global connectivity and digital transformation.

item.title: Beaujolais nouveau 2026: a fresh, light vintage hopes to revive a struggling sector
item.description: The party to celebrate the 2026 vintage of Beaujolais nouveau, said this year to be fruity, light and easy to drink: the ideal recipe for forgetting the sector’s crisis.

item.title: Islam to become world's largest religion by 2035 as Christianity also grows, study says
item.description: Pew Research Center has projected that both Islam and Christianity will grow between 2020 and 2070, with Muslims rising by more than 80% to over 3.6 billion and Christians by 30% to close to 3 billion.

item.title: AI being run in a 'medieval' way, says UN rights chief
item.description: UN high commissioner for human rights Volker Türk warned that while AI might sound something futuristic, underneath it is based on an age-old narrative of power.

item.title: EU moves towards 10-year probation period for new members - starting with Montenegro
item.description: EU ambassadors broadly backed a 10-year probation period for newcomers, with voting rights open to suspension for Orbán-style breaches, as a basis for Montenegro’s treaty.

item.title: EU must move beyond piecemeal trade deals with China, MEPs warn
item.description: MEPs are calling on the European Commission to “ease” the regulatory burden on EU companies and deploy “horizontal” trade defence tools to tackle Chinese competition.

item.title: Damaged buildings and debris after Ukrainian attack on Russia's Kursk
item.description: At least 11 people were injured after a Ukrainian attack damaged residential buildings and public facilities in the southwestern Russian city of Kursk, according to regional Governor Alexander Khinshtein.

item.title: Weakened Putin is pinning his hopes on a Le Pen victory, Browder says
item.description: Kremlin critic Bill Browder tells Euronews that a weakened Vladimir Putin is using peace talks to buy time, hoping a far-right victory in France will fracture European support for Ukraine.

item.title: Ukraine peace deal 'not feasible' without Europe, Polish minister warns
item.description: Poland’s Deputy Foreign Minister Ignacy Niemczycki tells Euronews that Europe is indispensable to any Ukraine peace settlement, hinting that Kyiv’s allies are moving towards a military role in enforcing an agreement.

item.title: Dutch embassy in Kyiv damaged by a projectile crash nearby
item.description: A projectile struck the area behind the Dutch embassy in Ukraine on Thursday, causing minor damage to the building; no casualties were reported.

item.title: Doing More with Less: Why Cost-Effective AI Agents Are European SMEs’ Hidden Asset in Global Trade
item.description: As European SMEs embrace AI, Alibaba.com's Accio shows how agentic tools can bridge the productivity gap, easing expansion and routine e-commerce tasks.

item.title: How much does sick leave cost Europe, and which countries take the most?
item.description: Sickness absence costs the EU up to €810 billion every year, highlighting the need for better prevention and earlier treatment to reduce its economic impact, a new report has found.

item.title: Serbia's student movement takes another step towards power with parliament speaker election
item.description: Aleksandar Čupić's appointment marks a historic breakthrough for the grassroots movement, which ended 14 years of rule by Aleksandar Vučić's party after campaigning against corruption.

item.title: Plenty of healthy people are low on iron. Here’s why it gets missed
item.description: Many people with iron deficiency aren’t diagnosed right away.

item.title: Putin hails ‘new chapter in the history of diplomacy’ after talks with Trump
item.description: Vladimir Putin says his meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping covered key global security issues, including the war in Ukraine, nuclear proliferation and freedom of navigation. The leaders also discussed maritime law, the role of the International Criminal Court and potential UN reforms.

item.title: FIFA U-17 World Cup opens in Qatar as four European nations make tournament debuts
item.description: European champions Italy and four European debutants are among the 48 teams taking part, while last year’s finalists Portugal and Austria are absent. Qatar is hosting the second of five consecutive editions from 2025 to 2029. The final is on 13 December.

item.title: This country’s AI ambitions: From public services to global markets
item.description: Azerbaijan is pursuing regional AI ambitions through digital public services, stronger data infrastructure, skills development and businesses targeting international markets.

item.title: Data centre energy consumption could double by 2030 straining grids, IEA warns
item.description: Data centres could use roughly 1,000 terawatt-hours of power annually by 2030 under the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) Stated Policies Scenario.

item.title: French Comté crowned world's best at the 2026 World Cheese Awards
item.description: A 24-month-aged cheese from France's Jura mountains has won the top prize at the 2026 World Cheese Awards, beating more than 5,300 entries from 45 countries.

item.title: 'COP31 has been muzzled': Latest draft deal scrubs all mention of fossil fuels
item.description: The transition away from fossil fuels (TAFF) has become a flashpoint discussion at the annual UN climate summit.

item.title: 'It's surreal': US gamers get their first taste of long-awaited GTA VI
item.description: Gamers in Miami celebrated the midnight launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, ending a 13-year wait for the latest instalment of the hugely successful franchise. Some fans even took time off work to experience the game, which recreates a virtual version of Miami.

item.title: Ukraine strikes key bridge linking Russia and Crimea for third time this week, halting rail traffic
item.description: The Russian transport ministry said on Thursday that no one was wounded in the attack and that train services across it had been temporarily halted.

item.title: Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya UN court rules
item.description: The International Court of Justice ruled by nine votes to six that Myanmar had "committed" genocide against the Rohingya community.

item.title: UK inflation hits 12-month high: What's driving the rise in prices?
item.description: Britain's inflation rate edged up in October to its highest level in 12 months, official data showed on Wednesday. So what's driving the increase?

item.title: Italy approves antisemitism law amid protests from left-wing opposition
item.description: The Chamber finally approved an anti-antisemitism bill using the IHRA definition, splitting the opposition and reviving debate on where criticism of Israel's government ends and antisemitism begins.

item.title: Portuguese families could spend 83% of average net income on rent, study finds
item.description: Among 20 Portuguese cities studied by the property listings website Idealista, Faro was the least affordable for renters and Funchal for buyers. In Lisbon, advertised rents equalled 88% of the average net household income and estimated mortgage repayments 90%.

item.title: EU pushes methane rules back two years in win for oil and gas industry
item.description: MEPs and EU governments have agreed to postpone key methane emissions requirements by two years amid pressure from the fossil fuel industry and mounting concerns over energy security and affordability.

item.title: Corrado Augias dies aged 91, journalism world mourns, minute of silence in Senate
item.description: A leading figure in Italian journalism for decades, the journalist Corrado Augias has died at the age of 91.

item.title: Commerzbank welcomes UniCredit commitments after Berlin agreement
item.description: Commerzbank has welcomed UniCredit's commitments to keep the German lender listed and based in Frankfurt. This comes as Berlin and UniCredit have agreed on key terms of what would be one of Europe's biggest cross-border banking deals in years.

item.title: US President Trump rejects global AI regulation as China's Xi calls for cooperation on safety
item.description: The US and Chinese leaders have set out contrasting approaches to AI governance at talks in Shenzhen, with Trump warning that regulation could hamper innovation while Xi called for the technology to remain under human control.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 19th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 19th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Ocean Catalyst Group launched at COP31 to safeguard ‘vital’ coastal and marine tourism
item.description: At COP31 in Türkiye, the World Travel & Tourism Council and member organisations launched the Ocean Catalyst Group to drive investment, strengthen coastal resilience and protect marine destinations.

item.title: Smooth as silk: how Thai Airways is rebuilding the road between Europe and Asia
item.description: Thai Airways is growing again, adding more European flights via Bangkok and upgrading cabins, food and service to deliver a smoother, more connected journey.

item.title: Spain freezes new foreign degree applications as foreign doctors flood residency exam
item.description: A Spanish ministry has stopped accepting new applications to recognise foreign university degrees, after years of increases.

item.title: From car parts to drones: German suppliers pivot to defence as auto crisis deepens
item.description: German car parts makers are moving into drones, defence and space as the country's auto industry crisis deepens, with one Bavarian family firm now able to turn out 1,000 surveillance drones every month as it tries to depend less on carmakers.

item.title: EU Commission hit by large-scale cyberattack with data leakage unknown
item.description: The European Commission's internal HR systems have been targeted by an AI-powered cyberattack, with EU cyber experts still assessing whether sensitive personal information has been compromised.

item.title: Gender pay gap: French women mark symbolic 'unpaid' day on 19 November
item.description: French women will symbolically start working for free from 10:51 am on November 19, according to feminist newsletter Les Glorieuses. The calculation highlights a 21.8% pay gap between women and men in France.

item.title: Danish lawmakers ratify US-Greenland security pact
item.description: The deal lets the United States build two new military bases on the Arctic island and stays in force even if Greenland becomes independent.
